note: Each entry is a directly-linked pair (Jaccard similarity of token sets, stopwords kept, >= the stated threshold) of titles from different domains, where (a) their single-linkage cluster at that threshold spans >=3 distinct domains -- i.e. it is a cluster that actually counts toward Echo index B, not one discarded by Rule B's own domain bar -- and (b) at least one of the two titles does not individually belong to any Rule A echo phrase. 'caught_by_rule_a_1/2' indicates whether that specific title individually belongs to a Rule A echo, so a reader can see which side of the pair (if either) Rule A already caught. Ordering is deterministic: similarity descending, then by the lexicographically smaller url in the pair. Each threshold entry carries an explicit 'count' field; count 0 with an empty 'examples' list is a reported finding (no qualifying pair existed at that threshold), not a gap in the data.
